title: Wang2026: Sensory-guided joint-learning MI-BCI study from Wang et al. (2026)
description: EEG recordings from 39 healthy, BCI-naive participants in a longitudinal motor imagery brain-computer interface study of sensory-guided human-machine joint learning. Participants performed online 1D and 2D cursor control using left-hand, right-hand, bilateral-hand and rest imagery across multiple sessions. Cohorts received joint learning with tactile guidance and EEGNet adaptation, fixed BCI2000 decoding, tactile-only control, or EEGNet-only control. Data comprise 62-channel EEG sampled at 1000 Hz.
methods_description: 62-channel EEG was recorded with a Compumedics Neuroscan SynAmps 2/RT amplifier and Quik-Cap at 1000 Hz, referenced midway between Cz and CPz, with a 60 Hz notch filter. Stimulus presentation and online control used BCI2000. Each regular session contained six runs, plus a separate initial BCI2000 baseline run. Subjects completed 4, 6, or 8 sessions with visual cursor feedback, tactile guidance, and EEGNet or BCI2000 decoding depending on cohort.
